clue.text: Bag carrier is responsible for carriage

parts.note: someone who shoulders a burden bears responsibility for it
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: A porter who is in charge of transporting luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: The band over a shoulder holds up a handbag or satchel, so it carries the bag.

clue.text: One who can't help taking an interest in your business

definitions.text: One who can't help taking an interest in your business

parts.words: One who can't help taking an interest in your business
parts.note: reads like a nosy busybody, but means an investor who takes a financial stake while giving no help in running the firm

explanation.surface: A meddler who is compulsively curious about your affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can't help' seems to mean 'cannot resist'; here it means the person gives no assistance, and 'interest' is a share of the profits.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of investor puts capital into a firm and draws profit but plays no active part in managing it.

clue.text: Device for measuring fingers

parts.note: suggests a gauge for hand sizes, but fingers are tots of spirits, measured out in a pub by a dispenser fixed to an upturned bottle

explanation.surface: A tool for sizing someone's hand, as a glove-maker might use.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'finger' of whisky is a measure the depth of a finger; British pubs pour spirits through an inverted-bottle dispenser giving a fixed measure.
explanation.definitionFit: This pub dispenser attached to a bottle releases an exact measure of spirit each time it is pressed.

clue.text: Braggart making an ostentatious entrance

parts.note: loud clothes or decor are showy and ostentatious
a mouth is an opening or entrance, as of a cave or river

explanation.surface: A boaster who makes a showy arrival at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart talks boastfully and too much, which is exactly what a blowhard noisy talker does.

clue.text: Russian republic's note on Nato is ill-disposed

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another comes above it, so first

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: badly disposed, so the letters of these words are arranged wrongly into a new order

explanation.surface: A Soviet republic's note to the Western alliance is hostile in tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-disposed' rearranges NATO IS into STONIA, placed under E. The clue dates from Soviet times, when the Baltic state was one of the Soviet republics; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic state was a constituent republic of the Soviet Union, loosely called Russia, until 1991.

clue.text: That is a sign to make your getaway

parts.note: sc. abbreviates Latin scilicet, meaning 'that is to say' or namely
the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A signal telling someone it is time to run off.
explanation.walkthrough: SC (scilicet) is a less familiar Latin abbreviation alongside i.e.; the Ram is the zodiac sign Aries.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang imperative 'clear off!' means leave quickly, so to bolt or flee.

clue.text: Fat beast accepting direction to diet

indicators.note: the first word takes in the next piece, holding it inside

parts.note: fat food is rich food
E is east, a compass direction
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A plump animal being put on a slimming regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' is not a slimming regime but a legislative assembly; German parliaments have been called diets.
explanation.definitionFit: The German parliament building and the imperial assembly it housed is the classic example of a national legislative assembly called a Diet.

clue.text: It may help writer to develop a point

definitions.text: It may help writer to develop a point

parts.words: It may help writer to develop a point
parts.note: sounds like aid in building an argument, but literally a gadget that gives a pencil a sharp tip

explanation.surface: Something that assists an author in elaborating an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: This desk gadget shaves wood and graphite to put a fine tip on the writing implement.

clue.text: Church officer, a Scot perhaps

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Lt is lieutenant, an army officer

explanation.surface: A church official who might be from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots, like the Irish and Welsh, are a Gaelic-speaking people of the ancient Celtic race, so one is an example.

clue.text: Perfect voice

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, complete or absolute, as in total nonsense
as a verb, to say or express aloud

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective meaning absolute and a verb meaning to speak out.

clue.text: Pubs where they call people to the bar

definitions.text: where they call people to the bar
definitions.meaning: the four London legal societies of Court admit barristers by calling them to the Bar

explanation.surface: Taverns where drinkers are summoned to the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar is not the pub counter but the legal profession; a barrister in England is 'called to the Bar' by one of the Inns of Court.
explanation.definitionFit: Taverns are hostelries; the Inns of Court are the legal societies that admit barristers.

clue.text: Individual beginning to stick mice back into cage

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word means just its opening letter
the reversed word goes inside the enclosure word

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

indicators.note: back tells us the word mice is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Someone starts sticking mice back into their cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' and 'cage' paint a pet-keeping scene; the stick is just a word supplying its first letter, and the cage an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: One example taken from a class, such as a sample animal or plant, is a single item or individual.

clue.text: Light material in twinkling musical

parts.note: a twinkling is a moment, a mo
Hair is a 1960s rock musical

explanation.surface: Lightweight fabric appears in a sparkling stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: This fabric is woven from Angora goat hair and is a fine, light textile.

clue.text: Elected junior minister admitting bill is defective

indicators.note: the combined words let the next piece in between them

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in
a curate is an assistant clergyman, a junior minister of religion
AC is account, a bill

explanation.surface: A newly elected junior government minister lets in a flawed bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junior minister' suggests government, but a curate is a junior minister of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Something defective is faulty, and a faulty figure or statement is wrong or erroneous.

clue.text: Carry revolver in exercise

parts.note: to cart is to carry or convey
a wheel revolves, turning round

explanation.surface: Bearing a handgun during military drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' suggests a gun; it is anything that turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The sideways handspring over the hands is a gymnastic exercise.

clue.text: French bookmaker -the last to be index-linked?

definitions.text: French bookmaker -the last to be index-linked?

parts.words: French bookmaker -the last to be index-linked?
parts.note: a bookmaker is not a turf accountant but a novelist from France, whose surname starts with the alphabet's final letter, so last in an alphabetical index

explanation.surface: A Paris betting shop owner whose odds rise with inflation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' and 'index-linked' suggest betting and finance; a writer surnamed with Z would come last in an index of authors.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Germinal and J'accuse was a nineteenth-century French novelist, literally a maker of books.

clue.text: Examination in French is on time

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece on another follows it

parts.note: est is French for is

explanation.surface: A French exam is held on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a trial of knowledge or ability.

clue.text: Box a Pole

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to box lightly in practice
a stout pole, as used for a mast or boom on a ship

explanation.surface: Fight a man from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole's capital letter suggests a Polish person; it is just a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers practise in rounds against a partner; a ship's mast or boom is a pole of this name.

clue.text: Shopping madam carries in a fury

indicators.note: the phrase holds the letters within it, carrying them across its words

explanation.surface: A woman out shopping lugs her bags around in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being furious is informally called jumping up and down with anger.

clue.text: Pedestrian pressure on car, so I got out

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece on top comes first

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics

indicators.note: the letters escape their order and come out differently arranged

explanation.surface: A walker presses against a car and climbs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got out' rearranges CAR SO I into ROSAIC, under P. 'Pedestrian' suggests a walker but means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian writing or ideas are dull and lacking imagination, unpoetic.

clue.text: Organised sailors sounding coarse

indicators.note: the word for coarse spoken aloud matches the answer

parts.note: crude means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: Sailors who were arranged and talked in a vulgar way.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has been manned has had its hands arranged and allocated, staffed with seamen.

clue.text: Italian magistrate arresting Duke for trick

indicators.note: the outer word holds the next piece inside, as a police officer holds a suspect

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa
D is duke

explanation.surface: A Venetian judge detains a nobleman for deceit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a crafty ploy or ruse.

clue.text: Too late to pick River Po trip before end of June

indicators.note: a trip is a fall or stumble, so these letters tumble into a new order
the end of the next word means just its last letter

explanation.surface: A Po river journey taken before the end of June is past its moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' looks like a journey on the river; it rearranges RIVER PO into OVERRIP, followed by E.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit past its best has gone soft, so it is beyond the time for harvest.

clue.text: Deny sending up King Edward, for one

indicators.note: in a down clue sending a word up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: a King Edward is a British variety of potato, which is a tuber

explanation.surface: Refuse to mock the monarch Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato variety; 'sending up' sounds like mockery but reverses the word in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny an accusation is to refute it with argument.

clue.text: Part of limb that may be bent in a submission

definitions.text: Part of limb that may be bent in a submission

parts.words: Part of limb that may be bent in a submission
parts.note: points to the leg joint people go down on when bowing in homage or surrender

explanation.surface: A wrestler's arm locked in a submission hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submission' suggests a wrestling hold; it is deference, as when a subject goes down before a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The leg joint bends when one kneels in homage or submission.

clue.text: Severe lawgiver to take action about motorists

indicators.note: the first word goes round the next piece

parts.note: to do is to act
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A harsh legislator moves against drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British motoring association for motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian legislator gave his name to harsh laws, hence 'draconian'.

clue.text: Fringe report

definitions.meaning: a fringe of hair cut straight across the forehead, US usage
the loud sound of a gun going off

explanation.definitionFit: Hair cut across the brow is called this in America; a gunshot's loud sound is also so named.

clue.text: Big dipper using paint-spreader with protective mat

parts.note: a roller spreads paint on walls
a coaster is a small mat protecting a table from a glass

explanation.surface: A decorator rolls paint with a mat to protect the furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big dipper' is the British name for a fairground ride, not the star group.
explanation.definitionFit: A big dipper is the British term for the fairground railway with steep drops.
